C1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
C1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the norm-one cycle fixes no line of the shell plane, and the cycle fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the norm-one cycle, is never registered alone.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.scalar_of_im_zero
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the two scalars `±1` are the only norm-one elements with `b = 0`: `a² = 1` forces `a = ±1`.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.split_fixed_lines
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the split torus `diag(g, g⁻¹)` fixes exactly the two coordinate lines of the projective line: a point `[x : y]` is fixed iff `g x · y = x · g⁻¹ y`, i.e. `(g² − 1) x y = 0`, i.e. `x y = 0` since `g² ≠ 1` (the drive is primitive of order `p − 1 > 2`). The photon's two helicities, residue `2`.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.centre_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the arithmetic of the centre's order formula. Given that the centre of `SU(3, 𝔽_q)` is the norm-one cube roots of unity, `gcd(3, q + 1)` of them (27-fields Proposition su3, imported, not proved here), on every shell of the sweep below `200`, `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` gives `Z₃` and `q ≡ 1 (mod 12)` the trivial centre, and the residue `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is exactly `q ≡ 1 (mod 4)` (a shell) with `q ≡ 2 (mod 3)` (the centre of order three). Kernel-decided over the range, so that no library lemma on `gcd` or `%` (which carry `propext`) enters.

C2.doc: 46:C2 — the laboratory Subjects: `173 ≡ 5 (mod 12)` has the centre `Z₃`; `13` and `1549`, both `≡ 1 (mod 12)`, have the trivial centre.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.carrier_triality
C2.doc: 46:C2, 46:B5 — colour's triality is the Carrier's relation: each of the three laboratory Carriers is `5 (mod 12)`, so `3` divides `Ω + 1` and not `Ω − 1`. The cube roots of unity are the pairs `(0, 1)` and `(−1, −1)` of residues, `a + bω` with `ω² = −ω − 1` and the norm `a² − ab + b²`: both have norm `1`, `(0, 1)² = (−1, −1)` and `(0, 1)·(−1, −1) = (1, 0)`. The product of `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` is `(ac − bd, ad + bc − bd)`.

C3.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
C3.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimir_exponents
C4.doc: 46:C4 — the Casimir rationals from the frame's torus exponents, with no lift (round 03, 9 November 2026). A torus element of the unitary frame acts on the fundamental with the eigenvalue exponents `(a, b, −a−b)` and on the adjoint with their six differences and two zeros; the second moment of the adjoint's exponents is six times the fundamental's, `2((a−b)² + (2a+b)² + (a+2b)²) = 6(a² + b² + (a+b)²)`, which is `T_A/T_F = 6` and hence `C_A/C_F = 9/4`. On the Subject `13` the split torus has the exponents `(n, 12n, −13n)` modulo `168`: `2((11n)² + (14n)² + (25n)²) = 6(n² + (12n)² + (13n)²)` for every `n < 168` (`1884 n² = 6 · 314 n²`); at `n = 1` likewise on `173` (`(1, 172, −173)`) and `1549` (`(1, 1548, −1549)`). The identity for every exponent pair is the Mathlib cell `YangMillsML.casimir_exponents_all`.

C14.doc: 46:C14 — the series' window, the corollary of A9 (the push on T06, 9 November 2026). C16.name: FRC.YangMills.frame_cycle_trace
C16.doc: 46:C16 — the second cycle on the three Subjects, in the arithmetic of the plane `F_p(√2)` alone, for a matrix with the characteristic polynomial of a generator of that cycle: the companion matrix `C` of `x³ − t x² + t̄ x − 1`, `t = (9, 4)`, `(166, 160)`, `(1275, 523)`. A frame element with this characteristic polynomial is conjugate to `C` over the plane, and the statements do not change under conjugation. `C` has the order `p² − p + 1 = 157`, `29757`, `2397853` (a power `C^(m/r)` is not `1` for the prime divisors `r` of `m`) and no eigenvalue on the plane. `C`, `C^(p²)` and `C^(−p)` are the three roots of the polynomial: their sum is `t·1`, the sum of their pairwise products `t̄·1` and their product `1`, so `C^k + C^(kp²) + C^(−kp) = (Tr C^k)·1` for every power. On `173` the power `C^(m/3)` is the central point `(86, 155)` of order `3`.

C17.name: FRC.YangMills.instance_amplitude
C17.doc: 46:C17 — the instance's distribution: the values `3, 3z, 3z²` on `64` elements each and `0` on `24` sum to zero, `64 · (3 + 3z + 3z²) = 0`; every nonzero value has norm `9`, so the moments are `192 · 9 / 216 = 8`, `192 · 27 / 216 = 24` (the cubes of `3, 3z, 3z²` are all `27`) and `192 · 81 / 216 = 72`; the invariant counts the moments are set against are `1, 1, 2`.

C18.name: FRC.YangMills.instance_transfer
C18.doc: 46:C18 — the transfer tally on the instance, the step of one plaquette with the frame's mean: the multiplicities `9, 36, 144, 27` of the eigenvalues `2/3, 1/6, 0, −1/3` sum to `216`; the eigenvalues are the integers `144, 36, 0, −72` of the matrix `216 K` over `216`; with the denominators cleared by `6` the trace is `tr K = 3`, and by `36` it is `tr K² = 8`, which is the sum `192 · 9` of the norms of the `216` amplitudes over `216`; `(3x + 1)(6x − 1)(3x − 2) = 54x³ − 27x² − 9x + 2`, so the annihilating polynomial has distinct roots; and `−1/3 < 0`.

C19.name: FRC.YangMills.subject_spectrum
C19.doc: 46:C19 — the transfer tally on the Subjects: the orders `811 273 008`, `802 332 524 681 473 968`, `33 144 476 289 365 359 469 790 000` of the frames on `13`, `173`, `1549`; the degrees `157, 2198, 2352`; `29 757, 5 177 718, 5 207 472`; `2 397 853, 3 716 672 150, 3 719 070 000`, whose inverses with the signs `+, +, −` are the eigenvalues of the step with the frame's mean; and the bookkeeping of the spectrum on each.

C19.name: FRC.YangMills.degree_identity
C19.doc: 46:C19 — the identity `Σ a χ(1) = 3 = w(1)` swept over `1 ≤ q ≤ 2000`.

C20.name: FRC.YangMills.ring_gap
C20.doc: 46:C20 — the gap of the transfer tally is `1/(q + 1)` on the seven frames of 46:C19: `1/14`, `1/174`, `1/1550` on the Subjects.

C20.name: FRC.YangMills.ring_tally_plane
C20.doc: 46:C20 — the reduced tally of the ring on pairs `a + b√ν`, for every modulus `p` and every `ν`; for a nonsquare `ν` of a Subject the pairs are its quadratic extension `K`. The six arguments are reduced character values that take at `h⁻¹` the conjugate of their value at `h`; that they do is the table's identity, checked class by class in the ledger file. (1) The conjugate of the reduced tally is the tally formed at the conjugate values. (2) The product of the two is the norm of the reduced tally, an element of the shell.

C20.name: FRC.YangMills.ring_tally_outside_shell
C20.doc: 46:C20 — the tally of the ring at a boundary class with eigenvalues outside the shell, on the three Subjects, in `K = F_p(√2)` on pairs `(a, b) = a + b√2`. (1) `2` is a nonsquare, by Euler's criterion, and the residues of `2⁻¹`. (2) The eigenvalues `√2`, `−√2/2`, `−1` of `h₂`: their product is `1`, the second is the inverse of the conjugate of the first, the third times the first is its conjugate, and the first plus the second is `√2/2`. (3) The reduced tally is `−1 − (5/4)√2`: `(12, 2)`, `(172, 42)`, `(1548, 386)`, outside the shell, with the second coordinate the residue of `−5/4`. (4) Its norm, the reduced paired weight, is `6`, `106`, `966`, the residue of `−17/8`. Every power is taken by repeated multiplication of residues.

C21.name: FRC.YangMills.spectrum_in_pi
C21.doc: 46:C21 — the spectrum in `2π = p − 1` on the three Subjects, `π = 6, 86, 774`: `d₁ = 4π² + 2π + 1`, `d₂ = (2π + 2) d₁` and `d₃ = 8π(π + 1)²`, so the gap of the transfer tally is `1/(2π + 2)`; and `2π + 2` has the residue `1` on the shell.

C21.name: FRC.YangMills.gap_at_classical_pi
C21.doc: 46:C21 — `YangMillsML.gap_at_classical_pi`: the gap `1/(2π + 2)` of the transfer tally read at the classical `π`, in `(0.12072, 0.12073)`.

C22.name: FRC.YangMills.product_channel_counts
C22.doc: 46:C22 — the product channels, the arithmetic of the counts. The binomial inversion of the compact counts `1, 1, 2, 6, 23` gives the fixed dimensions `0, 1, 2, 8` of `8^{⊗n}` on a Subject, and of the instance's counts `1, 1, 2, 11, 92` gives `7` and `57`. A fixed subspace of dimension `2` has `p² + 1` invariant lines, `170`, `29930`, `2399402` on the Subjects; on the instance `(4^d − 1)/3` gives `5`, `5461`, `21845` for `d = 2, 7, 8`; and the degree `8` lies in the window `2p − 1` of the Subject `13`.

C23.name: FRC.YangMills.uniform_boundary_tally
C23.doc: 46:C23 — the tally of the ring with the same boundary links at every step, of the eigenvalues `g^{±j}, 1` and `g^{±k}, 1` with `g = 2` and `(j, k) = (1, 2)`; after `n` steps the boundary classes are those of `x = 2^n` and `y = 4^n`. (1) The inverses of `2` and `4` on the three Subjects. (2) On `13` the tally at the lengths `1` to `12`. (3) On the Subjects `13`, `173`, `1549` the tally is the five powers at every regular length of the drive's cycle. (4) The other lengths: four on each Subject, the multiples of `3`, `43` and `387`. (5) At the length of the cycle the boundary links are units and the tally is `3`. Every product is reduced at once; the largest numeral formed is the degree `(p + 1)²(p − 1)`.

C24.name: FRC.YangMills.window_readings
C24.doc: 46:C24 — what a reading keeps of the window. (1) The pair `(1, 13)` has `13!/(840 · 120 · 24) = 2574 = 13 · 198` invariants (the hook formula on `(5, 4, 4)`), so the count reads `0` on the Subject `13`. (2) On the Subjects `13`, `173`, `1549` the factorial `(p − 1)!` reads `p − 1`, and `2` and `3` have inverses: the factors `2`, `3` and `1, …, p − 1` of the denominators of the series' coefficients below `ϑ^p` are units of the shell, and these coefficients are computed in its arithmetic. (3) `p!` reads `0`: from `ϑ^p` on no reading is stated.

C25.name: FRC.YangMills.three_rings_reading
C25.doc: 46:C25 — three rings on common links, each with the same boundary link at every step, of the eigenvalues `g^{±j}, 1` with `g = 2` and `j = 1, 2, 3`; after `n` steps the boundary classes are those of `2^n`, `4^n` and `8^n`. (1) The inverses of `8` on the three Subjects. (2) The count of invariants of the second character alone, `p` on `13` and `1549` and `3p` on `173`, has the residue `0`. (3) On `13` the regular lengths and their residues. (4) On the Subjects `13`, `173`, `1549` the tally is the expression at every regular length of the drive's cycle. (5) The first length reads `6`, `25` and `616`. Every product is reduced at once.

C26.name: FRC.YangMills.shell_series_readings
C26.doc: 46:C26 — the series on the shell. (1) The integers `h_k` of `3c₃` and of `8c₈` for `k < 8`, from the counts. (2) `p!` reads `0` on the three laboratory Subjects, so the `p`-th power of the stiffness reads `0` in the divided-power algebra of the series. (3) On the Subject `13` at channel unity the sum of the coefficients of `c₃` below `ϑ¹³` reads `6`, and the quotient of the two truncated sums reads `4`.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
X1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the norm-one cycle fixes no line of the shell plane, and the cycle fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the norm-one cycle, is never registered alone.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_no_invariant
X1.doc: 46:X1 — the adjoint has no invariant: `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` has one singlet (the trace) and the adjoint `𝟠` is its complement, `E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`; with `no_shell_eigenvalue` (the torus fixes no line) no registration singles a gluon out.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.residue_series_pieri
X2.doc: 46:X2 — one invariant line each: baryon `E[χ³] = 1`, meson `E[χχ̄] = 1`, glueball `E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, by the Pieri multiplicities.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
X2.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

X4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimirs
